triplets.head: HKDF
triplets.tail: Krawczyk's paper 'Cryptographic Extraction and Key Derivation: The HKDF Scheme', CRYPTO 2010

triplets.head: HKDF
triplets.tail: Two stages: HKDF-Extract (concentrate entropy) and HKDF-Expand (produce keying material)

triplets.head: HKDF-Expand
triplets.tail: T(n) = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T(n-1) | info | n); OKM = first L bytes of T(1)|T(2)|...

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 key schedule
triplets.tail: 3 stages: Early Secret (0-RTT), Handshake Secret, Master Secret

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: PSK from previous session's resumption_master_secret (no server contribution)

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: HKDF-Extract(0, PSK) → Early Secret → Derive-Secret(Early Secret, 'c e traffic', ClientHello) → client_early_traffic_secret

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: TLS does not provide inherent replay protections for 0-RTT data

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: No forward secrecy against PSK compromise

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: No replay protection at TLS layer

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: Direct Duplication — attacker copies 0-RTT flight and re-sends it

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: Cross-Zone Retry Exploitation (Gillmor Attack, 2015) — attacker sends ClientHello to multiple zones

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: Exhausting financial tolerances — replaying payment requests millions of times

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: Enhanced traffic analysis — millions of replays allow statistical de-anonymization of encrypted content

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: Single-Use Tickets — server maintains database of valid tickets, deletes after use

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT
triplets.tail: ClientHello Recording — server maintains time-windowed cache of seen ClientHellos

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 0-RTT

triplets.head: supported_versions extension
triplets.tail: Replaces legacy version negotiation entirely; client lists all supported TLS versions

triplets.head: supported_versions extension
triplets.tail: Server MUST use only this extension for version negotiation, ignoring ClientHello.legacy_version

triplets.head: supported_versions extension
triplets.tail: Client MUST check this extension before processing rest of ServerHello; abort with illegal_parameter if version not offered or prior to TLS 1.3

triplets.head: TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV

triplets.head: ServerHello Random Sentinel
triplets.tail: TLS 1.3 servers MUST set last 8 bytes of Random when negotiating lower version

triplets.head: ServerHello Random Sentinel
triplets.tail: TLS 1.3 clients MUST check last 8 bytes; if match found, abort with illegal_parameter alert

triplets.head: ServerHello Random Sentinel
triplets.tail: In TLS 1.2 with ephemeral ciphers, ServerKeyExchange includes signature over server_random; modifying random bytes invalidates signature

triplets.head: ServerHello Random Sentinel
triplets.tail: Does NOT provide protection when static RSA is used (no ServerKeyExchange message)

triplets.head: TLS 1.3
triplets.tail: Full Handshake Transcript Signature via CertificateVerify (RFC 8446 §4.4.3)

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify
triplets.tail: 64 bytes of 0x20 padding + context string ('TLS 1.3, server CertificateVerify' or 'TLS 1.3, client CertificateVerify') + 0x00 separator + Transcript-Hash(all handshake messages up to Certificate)

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify
triplets.tail: All cipher suite negotiations, key exchange group selections, extensions, both random values, server certificate

triplets.head: TLS 1.2 ServerKeyExchange
triplets.tail: Cipher suite selection, extensions, version field

triplets.head: TLS 1.3
triplets.tail: Finished Message MAC with strong HKDF-derived key (RFC 8446 §4.4.4)

triplets.head: TLS 1.3 Finished MAC
triplets.tail: MAC key derived via HKDF from (EC)DHE shared secret (strong), not from potentially weak negotiated parameters

triplets.head: TLS 1.2 Finished MAC
triplets.tail: MAC key derived from weak negotiated parameters; attacker who breaks weak params can forge MAC (circular dependency)

triplets.head: Bhargavan formal proof
